angleRead.name: Anthony Raines
angleRead.text: The story's in the numbers, but the weight's in the gloves being hung up. Ellis' six strong innings set the table, but the real meat is two franchise icons taking their last cuts in Keane and Dillon. That's where the human angle bites—not in the ERA, but in the equipment bags being packed for the last time. I'll start with the clubhouse attendants. They always know who's clearing out their locker before the players do.

plan.chase: The story's in the numbers, but the weight's in the gloves being hung up. Ellis' six strong innings set the table, but the real meat is two franchise icons taking their last cuts in Keane and Dillon. That's where the human angle bites—not in the ERA, but in the equipment bags being packed for the last time. I'll start with the clubhouse attendants. They always know who's clearing out their locker before the players do.
plan.focus: The transition moment—veterans exiting on top while the new core (Ellis, Taveras) carries the torch. Specifically how Ellis' bounce-back performance (6IP, 2ER) stabilized the series after his Game 2 stumble.
plan.why: Because championships get parades, but retirements get statues. The ledger shows Keane's 1 RBI and Dillon's final appearance, but the real story is the 27 combined seasons walking out that door.
checks: Verify with PR if Keane/Dillon made retirement announcements postgame
Cross-reference Ellis' Game 2 and Game 5 pitch mixes from the official scorer's report
Confirm Taveras' homer was off a lefty (career splits show .802 OPS vs LHP)
plan.interpretation: Paulson's seventh title cements his legacy, but the simultaneous passing of the torch (Ellis) and sunsetting of an era (Keane/Dillon) creates a rare trifecta of narrative angles within a single box score.
unverifiedLead: Clubhouse staff may have overheard Keane/Dillon discussing retirement plans during the celebration
Ellis' fastball velocity in Game 5 possibly rebounded to regular season levels after dipping in Game 2
plan.closeQuestion: Did Paulson intentionally script the bullpen to ensure both Keane and Dillon got ceremonial final appearances?
